note: Launch pads: stand on one and press E to fly the encounter it names. Read by src/systems/flow/game_flow.gd; the owning scene resolves 'town_box' (the pad sits on that box's footprint, at its base) and 'arrive_marker' (where the player lands back on foot, facing the pad) from its own layout data, so no coordinates live here or in code. Labels are here so code stays name-free. M14: the pit's ship is flown, not quick-launched: E boards it, and flying out of the atmosphere (the world's space_altitude) starts the pad's encounter. reentry_* place the ship back in the port's sky after space (altitude in metres, distance and bearing from the pad, nose pitch); reentry_delay is how long after a won fight before re-entry happens on its own. Issue #46: the pit's ship never leaves the town scene. Flying out of the atmosphere keeps you in the port's own sky; space_dogfight (on by default, F11 switches it) starts the pad's encounter right there (SpaceFight), and dropping space_exit_margin metres back below space_altitude breaks off a fight that is still running. reentry_* and reentry_delay now only apply to the stand-alone flight scene. seeker_alarm_secs: how long the cockpit's seeker warning (alarm, text, dash lamp) sounds when an enemy has a lock on you or a seeker in flight at you; seeker_alarm_rest: how long before it may go off again, if the threat is still there; seeker_lamp_hz: lamp flashes a second.

eject_note: Issue #275: hold B (flight_eject) for eject_hold seconds in the air, below space and outside a fight, to eject (ShipPilot.eject). You come out eject_clear_up metres over the ship's back and eject_clear_back behind her, rising at her climb plus eject_kick m/s, with her speed across the ground (at most eject_push_max m/s) carrying you on and fading by eject_push_fade m/s every second. Then you fall: falls hurt (content/core/flow/falls.json). The empty ship goes ADRIFT (issue #276, AtmoFlight): her adrift_gravity, adrift_drag and adrift_nose_rate come from the ship's atmosphere block, with defaults in code.
call_note: Issue #368: Call (the ledger's button by your primary ship) flies her to you with nobody at the controls and nobody chasing her (ShipPilot.call_ship). She lands on the nearest clear ground to where you called from: rings out to call_land_radius metres, a circle call_room metres across with no wall in it and no more than call_flat metres up or down, not on another ship; climbing onto a roof counts three times its height. She lifts off, climbs to call_cruise_agl over the ground (not moving across until she is clear of the roofs), comes across at up to call_speed m/s (call_climb m/s up or down), and from call_descend_at metres out drops to call_hold metres over the spot and lands. Already within call_near metres: she stays put. On another planet (or nowhere yet) she comes down out of the sky, call_from_height up and call_from_far across. Waking in the pit puts your primary on the pad, and whatever stood within call_pad_room metres of it moves to clear ground at least call_aside_min metres off.
bay_land_note: Issue #75: flying within bay_land_radius metres (across the ground) of your ship's bay, below space, Z flies her in and lands her on her own pad (ShipPilot.bay_land), on any planet.
